blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum! Aaj hum ek naya unit shuru kar rahe hain: Trigonometric Identities. Kitab kehti hai ke is unit mein hum pehle fundamental law of trigonometry (trigonometry ka bunyadi qanoon) saabit karenge, aur phir usi ki madad se Trigonometric Identities par baat karenge. Lekin us law ko saabit karne ke liye humein ek purana auzaar chahiye: plane mein do points ke darmiyan faasla (distance) nikalne ka formula. Is liye pehle usi ko taaza karte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Identity kya hoti hai? Identity aisi equation hai jo angle ki har value ke liye sach ho. Misaal ke taur par \(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1\): aap \(\theta\) ki jagah \(30^{\circ}\) rakhein, \(70^{\circ}\) rakhein ya koi bhi angle, jawab hamesha 1 aayega. Aam equation (jaise \(2x = 6\)) sirf ek khaas value par sach hoti hai, identity har value par.\nIs poore unit ki taqreeban har identity ek hi qanoon se nikalti hai: \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\) (topic 10.1.1). Us qanoon ka saboot ek circle ki do chords (circle ke do points ko milane wali seedhi lines) ki lambai ka muqabla kar ke diya jata hai, aur lambai naapne ke liye distance formula chahiye. Yeh hai is page ki ahmiyat.
Ab formula dekhte hain. Maan lijiye \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) aur \(Q(x_{2}, y_{2})\) do points hain, aur \(d\) un ke darmiyan faasla hai. To

blocks.text_alt: d equals the length of PQ equals the square root of (x1 minus x2) squared plus (y1 minus y2) squared

blocks.text: ya yeh bhi likh sakte hain:

blocks.text_alt: or d equals the square root of (x2 minus x1) squared plus (y2 minus y1) squared

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh formula aaya kahan se? Yeh asal mein Pythagoras theorem hi hai. \(P\) aur \(Q\) ko milayein aur ek right-angled triangle (samkon tikon) banayein jis ki ek side horizontal (leti hui) aur ek vertical (khari) ho. Horizontal side ki lambai \(|x_{2} - x_{1}|\) hai, vertical side ki \(|y_{2} - y_{1}|\), aur \(PQ\) hypotenuse (sab se lambi side, watar) hai. Pythagoras kehta hai: hypotenuse ka square = baqi do sides ke squares ka jama. Bas yahi formula hai.\nDono forms ek hi jawab kyun dete hain? Kyun ke \((x_{1} - x_{2})^{2} = (x_{2} - x_{1})^{2}\). Misaal: \((3 - 5)^{2} = (-2)^{2} = 4\) aur \((5 - 3)^{2} = 2^{2} = 4\). Square sign ko khatam kar deta hai, is liye pehle kaun sa point likhein, is se farq nahin parta.\nAur faasla kabhi negative nahin hota, is liye hum hamesha positive square root lete hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Points \((0, 0)\) aur \((3, 4)\) ka faasla zehan mein nikaaliye. (Ishara: \(3^{2} + 4^{2} = 25\).) Jawab 5 aaya? Shabash, yeh mashhoor 3-4-5 wala right triangle hai.

Ab kitab ki misaal dekhte hain. Is mein do hisse hain: pehle mein seedhe numbers hain, doosre mein coordinates trigonometric ratios ki shakal mein hain. Doosra hissa khaas taur par dhyan se dekhiye, kyun ke agle topic ka saboot bilkul isi tarah chalta hai.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.problem:
Find distance between the following points:
(i) \(A(3, 8)\), \(B(5, 6)\)
(ii) \(P(\cos x, \cos y)\), \(Q(\sin x, \sin y)\)
steps:
Given: (i) \(A(3, 8)\) aur \(B(5, 6)\); (ii) \(P(\cos x, \cos y)\) aur \(Q(\sin x, \sin y)\).
To find: har hisse mein dono points ka darmiyani faasla.
Method: sab se pehle hum dekhte hain ke sawal kya maang raha hai: do points ka faasla. Is ke liye distance formula \(d = \sqrt{(x_{1}-x_{2})^{2} + (y_{1}-y_{2})^{2}}\) bilkul fit hai, kyun ke use sirf dono points ke coordinates chahiye, aur woh humein diye hue hain. Plan: coordinates pehchaanein, formula mein rakhein, phir simplify karein.

Part (i), step 1: Coordinates pehchaanein
\[x_{1} = 3,\ y_{1} = 8\]
\[x_{2} = 5,\ y_{2} = 6\]
Kyun: chaaron numbers pehle alag likh lene se \(x\) wali value \(y\) wali value se ghalat mel nahin khati. Yeh chhoti si aadat bohat si ghaltiyon se bachati hai.

Part (i), step 2: Formula mein rakhein aur simplify karein
\[|AB| = \sqrt{(3-5)^{2} + (8-6)^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{(-2)^{2} + 2^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{4 + 4} = \sqrt{8}\]
\[= 2\sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: \((-2)^{2} = 4\), kyun ke negative number ka square positive hota hai. Phir \(\sqrt{8}\) ko simple karne ke liye 8 ko \(4 \times 2\) likhte hain; 4 perfect square hai, us ka root 2 bahar aa jata hai: \(\sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}\).\nDhyan dein: \(\sqrt{4 + 4}\) ko \(2 + 2\) mat likhiye. Pehle andar jama karein, phir root lein.

Part (ii), step 1: Coordinates pehchaanein
\[x_{1} = \cos x,\ y_{1} = \cos y\]
\[x_{2} = \sin x,\ y_{2} = \sin y\]
Kyun: coordinates numbers ki jagah trigonometric expressions hain, lekin ghabraane ki zaroorat nahin. Formula ko is se koi farq nahin parta; \(\cos x\) bhi bas ek number hi hai jis ki value \(x\) par munhasar hai.

Part (ii), step 2: Formula mein rakhein
\[|PQ| = \sqrt{(\cos x - \sin x)^{2} + (\cos y - \sin y)^{2}}\]
Kaam aasan karne ke liye pehle root ke andar wali cheez, yani \(|PQ|^{2}\), ko simplify karte hain:
\[|PQ|^{2} = (\cos x - \sin x)^{2}\]
\[\quad + (\cos y - \sin y)^{2}\]
Kyun: lamba square root har line mein saath ghaseetne se ghalti ka imkaan barhta hai. Pehle andar ka hisaab saaf karein, root aakhir mein ek hi dafa lein.

Part (ii), step 3: Har square ko kholein
\[(\cos x - \sin x)^{2}\]
\[= \cos^{2}x + \sin^{2}x - 2\cos x\sin x\]
\[(\cos y - \sin y)^{2}\]
\[= \cos^{2}y + \sin^{2}y - 2\cos y\sin y\]
Kyun: yahan algebra ka purana formula \((a - b)^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2} - 2ab\) laga hai, jahan \(a = \cos x\) aur \(b = \sin x\). Darmiyan wali term \(-2ab\) bhoolna aam ghalti hai.

Part (ii), step 4: \(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1\) istemal karein
\[\cos^{2}x + \sin^{2}x = 1,\ \cos^{2}y + \sin^{2}y = 1\]
\[|PQ|^{2} = 2 - 2\cos x\sin x - 2\cos y\sin y\]
\[= 2 - 2(\cos x\sin x + \cos y\sin y)\]
Kyun: chaar squared terms do jori ban jaati hain, aur har jori basic identity ke mutabiq 1 ke barabar hai, yani kul 2. Yahi woh jaadu hai jo agle topic ke saboot mein bhi kaam aayega. Aakhir mein aakhri do terms se 2 common nikaal liya, jaise kitab karti hai.

Part (ii), step 5: Square root lein
\[|PQ| = \sqrt{2 - 2(\cos x\sin x + \cos y\sin y)}\]
Kyun: faasla \(|PQ|^{2}\) ka positive square root hai. Kitab jawab isi shakal mein chhorti hai, aage simplify karne ki zaroorat nahin.

Tasdeeq:
(i) \(A(3, 8)\) se \(B(5, 6)\) tak jaane ke liye hum 2 unit daayen aur 2 unit neeche chalte hain. Yeh 2 side wale square ka diagonal hai, jis ki lambai \(2\sqrt{2}\) hoti hai. Jawab sahi hai.
(ii) Ek aasan value rakh kar dekhte hain: \(x = y = 0\). Tab \(P(1, 1)\) aur \(Q(0, 0)\), aur in ka faasla \(\sqrt{1 + 1} = \sqrt{2}\). Hamara jawab bhi \(\sqrt{2 - 2(0 + 0)} = \sqrt{2}\) deta hai. Dono barabar, yani jawab durust hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: points \(R(1, 2)\) aur \(S(4, 6)\) ka faasla nikaaliye.
\(x\) ka farq: \(4 - 1 = 3\); \(y\) ka farq: \(6 - 2 = 4\).
\(|RS| = \sqrt{3^{2} + 4^{2}} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5\).
Ab ulte order se: \(\sqrt{(1-4)^{2} + (2-6)^{2}} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5\). Wahi jawab! Is se saabit hua ke order se farq nahin parta.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) aur \(Q(x_{2}, y_{2})\) ka faasla: \(d = \sqrt{(x_{1}-x_{2})^{2} + (y_{1}-y_{2})^{2}}\).
2. Yeh formula Pythagoras theorem hi ki doosri shakal hai.
3. Tafreeq (subtraction) ka order maayne nahin rakhta, kyun ke farq ka square liya jata hai.
4. Coordinates trigonometric hon to \(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1\) dhoondiye; kaam aadha ho jata hai.
5. Agle topic (10.1.1) mein fundamental law isi formula se saabit hoga.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Har term ka alag root le lena: \(\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}} \ne a + b\). Misaal: \(\sqrt{4 + 4} = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.83\), jab ke \(2 + 2 = 4\). Bilkul alag!
2. \((-2)^{2} = -4\) likh dena. Negative number ka square hamesha positive hota hai: \((-2)^{2} = 4\).
3. \(x\)-coordinate ko \(y\)-coordinate se subtract kar dena. Hamesha \(x\) ko \(x\) se aur \(y\) ko \(y\) se jori banayein.
4. \((a - b)^{2}\) kholte waqt darmiyani term \(-2ab\) bhool jana.
